ui.universe.lab.title: Orbital laboratory: an experiment
ui.universe.lab.purpose: What if? Change the conditions, see what the science models say would follow, and compare it with the real solar system, which stays as it is.
ui.universe.lab.compare.title: Compared with the real {name}
ui.universe.lab.compare.unbound: No longer an orbit: it is escaping. In reality, {real} across the middle of its orbit.
ui.universe.lab.compare.note: A thought experiment: the real world goes on as it is.
ui.universe.lab.compare.prompt.mass: What changed? With a different mass, {name} pulls on everything near it differently: watch how its moons and neighbours respond.
ui.universe.lab.compare.prompt.size: What changed? The same mass in a different size: its surface gravity and density change, but its pull from far away does not.
ui.universe.lab.compare.prompt.wider: What changed? A wider orbit: a longer year, and less light from its star. Why does the year grow faster than the orbit?
ui.universe.lab.compare.prompt.tighter: What changed? A tighter orbit: a shorter year, and more light from its star. How close could it come before its star’s pull tears at it?
ui.universe.lab.compare.prompt.escaped: What changed? It is moving too fast to be held: no longer in orbit, it is leaving. How much slower would it need to go to stay?
ui.universe.lab.note: A copy of the system you were exploring, now moved by its own gravity, not JPL’s predictions. {seed}
ui.universe.lab.rates: Asked for {requested} a second, running at {achieved} a second (steps of {step} min).
ui.universe.lab.ratesSlow: Asked for {requested} a second, but only {achieved} a second is possible here (steps of {step} min).
ui.universe.lab.paused: Paused: the experiment’s clock has stopped.
ui.universe.lab.failure: The numbers stopped making sense, so the experiment paused at its last good checkpoint. Go back to a checkpoint, or reset.
ui.universe.lab.disrupted: {absorbed} torn apart by {survivor}’s tides inside its Roche limit, at {when}: {count} pieces and a ring of its dust
ui.universe.lab.climate.title: Climate
ui.universe.lab.climate.luminosityValue: {value} times the Sun’s (as a main-sequence star of its mass, Eker et al. 2018)
ui.universe.lab.climate.surfaceValue: {mean} on average; {min} to {max} across its latitudes, the day’s means
ui.universe.lab.climate.waterValue: could lie on {share}% of the surface
ui.universe.lab.climate.water.thin: none: its air is too thin (below water’s triple point)
ui.universe.lab.climate.water.none: none at its surface in this model
ui.universe.lab.climate.budyko: the Earth’s today, as North, Cahalan and Coakley’s model has it, with {forcing} W/m² added
ui.universe.lab.climate.grey: a grey atmosphere of infrared optical depth {tau}: parameterised, set to give today’s measured mean
ui.universe.lab.climate.noteBudyko: An energy balance model by latitude: sunlight in, heat out, carried toward the poles; ice where the year’s mean falls below −10 °C, which reflects more and can freeze the world over. Warmth takes years to follow a change.
ui.universe.lab.climate.noteGrey: An energy balance model by latitude, its greenhouse a grey atmosphere set to give today’s measured mean; its heat capacity and the heat its air carries are illustrative.
ui.universe.lab.climate.noteAirless: Airless: each latitude’s day-mean balance of sunlight and heat radiated; its noon under the star is hotter, its night far colder (not modelled).
ui.universe.lab.climate.scale: Violet below −120 °C, blue at −50 °C, pale blue at −20 °C, white at freezing, yellow at 17 °C, orange at 32 °C, red at 77 °C, dark red from 227 °C.
ui.universe.lab.rings.title: Rings and belts
ui.universe.lab.rings.intro: Test particles feel every body’s gravity but pull on nothing. So thousands cost what a few bodies would, and they never change the bodies’ paths: a belt that Jupiter stirs, a ring a passing world scatters. A gravitating ring is a dozen bodies that pull on one another and on everything else.
ui.universe.lab.rings.count: Particles in a ring or belt
ui.universe.lab.rings.add.ring: A ring about the chosen body
ui.universe.lab.rings.need: Choose a body for a ring about it.
ui.universe.lab.rings.decorative: Saturn’s rings are drawn from Cassini’s measurements and take no part in the experiment: decorative, not simulated.

ui.universe.lab.thrusting: A ship is burning: its rocket adds energy and momentum (the propellant it throws out carries the balance away, and the experiment does not follow it).
ui.universe.lab.ship.intro: A ship weighs nothing to the worlds: it falls as a grain of dust would, but carries a rocket. Its numbers are yours to set; the ones given are illustrative (the specific impulse a storable-propellant engine gives).
ui.universe.lab.ship.name: Its name
ui.universe.lab.ship.title: Its rocket
ui.universe.lab.ship.mass: {kg} kg with its propellant (to the worlds, nothing: it pulls on none of them)
ui.universe.lab.ship.readout: {fuel} kg of propellant left: {dv} m/s of change of speed, by the rocket equation. Thrust {thrust} N, specific impulse {isp} s.
ui.universe.lab.ship.dir.normal: Normal: square to its orbit’s plane, north
ui.universe.lab.ship.dir.antinormal: Anti-normal: square to its orbit’s plane, south
ui.universe.lab.ship.dir.radialOut: Radial out: away from the body
ui.universe.lab.ship.planHint: The path drawn ahead runs through every burn planned: plan one, see where it takes the ship, then let the time run.
ui.universe.lab.ship.burnNow: Now: {dv} m/s {direction} about {ref}, burning {duration} in all
ui.universe.lab.lesson.title: Lessons
ui.universe.lab.lesson.intro: Short lessons, each on its own experiment, set up from the start. Each has a few steps, each an edit you make with its button, and says beforehand what to look for and the number the physics expects.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.kepler.title: Kepler’s third law
ui.universe.lab.lesson.kepler.intro: A star and a planet. Kepler found, and Newton explained, that the square of a world’s year goes as the cube of its distance from its star.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.kepler.1: The planet goes round once every {period}, at {a} from its star.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.kepler.act2: Move it out to twice the distance
ui.universe.lab.lesson.kepler.2before: Twice as far, the law says its year will be 2 to the power 1.5, 2.83 times as long.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.kepler.2: Expected: {expected}. The experiment now gives {period}: {ratio} times as long.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.kepler.3: Farther out it moves more slowly: {now} now, against {before} before (a circular orbit’s speed goes as one over the square root of the distance: {expected} expected).
ui.universe.lab.lesson.escape.title: Escape speed
ui.universe.lab.lesson.escape.what: fast enough never to come back
ui.universe.lab.lesson.escape.intro: A star and a planet. At the square root of two times its circular speed, a body escapes its star’s pull for good.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.escape.1: The planet moves at {v} about its star; escape speed where it is: {escape}.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.escape.act2: Push it a little past escape speed
ui.universe.lab.lesson.escape.2before: The push will be the difference, along its motion.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.escape.2wait: Pushed {push}; its orbit is taking the change.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.escape.2: Pushed {push}: its orbit is open now (eccentricity {e}, more than 1), a hyperbola. It will not come back.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.escape.3: It is {distance} from the star, and going.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.hohmann.title: A Hohmann transfer
ui.universe.lab.lesson.hohmann.what: two burns to a higher orbit
ui.universe.lab.lesson.hohmann.intro: A ship in a low orbit about the Earth, going to the height where an orbit takes a day. Hohmann’s transfer does it with two burns: one to stretch the orbit out to the new height, one there to make it round.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.hohmann.1: The ship is {r1} from the Earth’s centre; the target, {r2}. The transfer needs {dv1} now and {dv2} at the far side. Its tanks hold {left}.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.hohmann.act2: Plan the first burn, prograde, now
ui.universe.lab.lesson.hohmann.2before: The first burn stretches the orbit: its far side will reach the target height.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.hohmann.2: Planned: {dv1} prograde. Its path ahead now reaches out to the target.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.hohmann.act3: Run the clock through the burn
ui.universe.lab.lesson.hohmann.3: The orbit’s far side: {apo} (the target: {target}). Once round it takes {period}.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.hohmann.act4: Round the orbit at its far side (the autopilot)
ui.universe.lab.lesson.hohmann.4none: The second burn waits for an orbit with a far side to round.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.hohmann.4: The autopilot’s burn: {dv} at the far side, which comes in {when}.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.hohmann.4done: The autopilot’s burn of {dv} at the far side is done.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.hohmann.act5: Run the clock to the far side and on
ui.universe.lab.lesson.hohmann.5: Its orbit now: {a} across the middle, eccentricity {e}, once round in {period}.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.roche.title: The Roche limit
ui.universe.lab.lesson.roche.what: where tides pull a moon apart
ui.universe.lab.lesson.roche.intro: The Earth and its Moon. Close enough to a world, the difference of its pull across a moon is more than the moon’s own gravity can hold together.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.roche.1: The Moon is {distance} from the Earth. The Earth’s Roche limit for it: {fluid} for a fluid moon, {rigid} for a rigid one.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.roche.act2: Move the Moon inside the limit
ui.universe.lab.lesson.roche.2before: It will be put on a round orbit at four fifths of the fluid limit.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.roche.2: The Moon is now {a} from the Earth: inside the limit.
ui.universe.lab.lesson.roche.3wait: Watch the history as the tides work ({count} bodies now).
ui.universe.lab.lesson.roche.3: Torn apart: the history says so, and the pieces and the ring of dust go on round the Earth ({count} bodies now).

ui.universe.lab.ship.circulariseShort: Rounding the orbit at its far side would take {dv} m/s: more than the propellant left can give.
ui.universe.lab.ship.to: Or to a round orbit this far from its centre (km)
ui.universe.lab.ship.transferText: An autopilot: {dv1} m/s {dir1} now, then {dv2} m/s {dir2} at the far side of the transfer orbit, {coast} later (a Hohmann transfer).
ui.universe.lab.ship.transferShort: That transfer would take {dv} m/s: more than the propellant left can give.
ui.universe.lab.ship.transferRound: A transfer starts from a round orbit: make this one round first (its eccentricity is {e}).
ui.universe.lab.ship.transferBusy: A transfer starts now, with no other burns planned: call those off first.
ui.universe.lab.ship.transferBelow: That is below the surface of {primary} ({radius} km from its centre).
